passage:
Hi Mark,

I'm incredibly frustrated with the response I received from your automated support system regarding my request for a registration refund. As you know, I purchased a "VIP Executive Pass" for the Global Innovators Summit back in January for $1,200. Unfortunately, due to the sudden cancellation of my international flight following the regional storm last week, it was physically impossible for me to attend the event in London.

When I checked your website's terms and conditions before purchasing, the "Force Majeure" clause explicitly stated that refunds would be issued in the event of documented travel disruptions beyond the attendee's control. I have already provided the official flight cancellation notice from the airline and a copy of the emergency weather advisory. Despite this, your billing department is claiming that because I didn't cancel my registration 30 days in advance, I am only eligible for a "Credit Voucher" for next year's event. This is completely useless to me, as I am moving to a different industry and will not be attending future summits.

Furthermore, I was specifically promised a one-on-one networking session with the keynote speaker, Dr. Aris, as part of my VIP package. Since that session was scheduled for the first morning of the conference, which I obviously missed, that part of the service was never rendered. I am essentially being charged over a thousand dollars for a service I could not access and a promise that wasn't kept.

I've been a loyal attendee for five years, but this experience has left a very sour taste in my mouth. I'm giving your team 48 hours to process a full refund to my original credit card. If I don't see a confirmation by Wednesday evening, I will have no choice but to initiate a chargeback through my bank and leave a detailed review of this situation on the industry forums. I'd much rather resolve this amicably, but the current "voucher-only" offer is an insult given the circumstances.

Please let me know by tomorrow morning if you can escalate this to a senior manager.

Best,
Julianne Moore

questions.prompt: Julianne's primary justification for a cash reversal hinges on ______.
options: The duration of her professional tenure.
A breach of the 30-day notice protocol.
The unavailability of the keynote speaker.

questions.prompt: The billing department's refusal is technically predicated on Julianne's ______.
options: Failure to meet a temporal prerequisite.

questions.prompt: Julianne argues that the contract is partially void because of ______.
options: A failure to deliver a specific engagement.
The airline's refusal to honor her ticket.
Mark's personal negligence in the matter.
An error in the automated support system.

questions.prompt: To satisfy the "Force Majeure" requirements, the sender has already ______.
options: Requested an escalation to Dr. Aris.
Authenticated the nature of the hindrance.
Reimbursed the bank for the chargeback.

questions.prompt: If Julianne's demand is ignored by Thursday, she intends to ______.
options: File a lawsuit against the airline.
Contact the original credit card company.

questions.prompt: Julianne's stance on the "Credit Voucher" implies that she ______.
options: Has already used the voucher once.

reply.text:
